summary: Cloudflare 2019 WAF regex backtracking is our 'never designed for' case: adversarial URL length, IDOR ids, and redirect floods. Transparency means publishing the leak body and the 404/429 matrix instead of a vague outage note.
evidence: Adversarial input here: (1) B guessing A's short_code — GET_A_AS_B 404 not 200 with URL; (2) create/redirect floods — 429 after 5 creates / 8 redirects; (3) missing owner filter on admin list leaked https://secret.example/a-private until FIX_IDOR_LEAK False. Error-handling analogue of CPU-saturating regex: a hung Postgres connect without timeout (Module 05 /ready hang) — we already mapped that to 503 rather than letting the worker sit at 100% wait.

Transparency: Cloudflare published the regex and timeline. Our IDOR postmortem is progress/system-design-module4-break.md with BREAK_LIST_B_BODY and the empty FIX_LIST_B_BODY. We also recorded persisted=memory instead of claiming a Postgres write while localhost:5432 is down — hiding that would be the 'brief disruption' version.
Canary lesson applied: rate limits and owner checks are in-process and proven on ASGI before any global deploy. Remaining: in-memory limiter is not a canary across workers.
